class CopilotAgent(AgentBase):

    MAX_ITERATIONS: int = 10

    def __init__(
        self,
        profile: AgentProfile,
        memory: MemoryController,
        context_engine: ContextAssembler,
        llm: LLMClient,
        tool_registry: ToolRegistry,
        telemetry: TelemetryProvider | None = None,
    ): ...

    async def run(self, input_signal: str) -> str:
        """Execute the Re-Act loop for a user query."""

    async def initialize_session(self) -> None:
        """Initialize a new session with memory priming."""

    async def archive_turn(self) -> None:
        """Archive the current turn to memory."""

from friday_memory import MemoryController

from friday_tools import DefaultToolRegistry

    memory=memory,
    context_engine=context_assembler,
    llm=LiteLLMService(model="gpt-4o-mini"),
    tool_registry=DefaultToolRegistry(),
)

await agent.initialize_session()
response = await agent.run("What files are in the current directory?")

class BaseTool(ABC):

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Unique tool identifier (lowercase_with_underscores)."""

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def description(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable description used by the LLM to decide when to call."""

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def parameters_schema(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """JSON Schema Draft 7 definition of the tool's parameters."""

    @property
    def category(self) -> str:
        """Tool category for filtering. Defaults to 'uncategorized'."""
        return "uncategorized"

    @property
    def tags(self) -> list[str]:
        """Optional tags for fine-grained filtering."""
        return []

    @abstractmethod
    async def execute(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
        """Execute the tool and return a string result."""

    def to_schema(self, format: str = "plain") -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Convert to LLM function-calling schema format."""

class MyCustomTool(BaseTool):

    @property
    def parameters_schema(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "type": "object",

                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "Text to transform",

            },
            "required": ["input"],

    async def execute(self, input: str) -> str:

registry = DefaultToolRegistry()
registry.register(MyCustomTool())

item.title: Protocol Specifications
item.description:
Full specification of every abstract protocol in friday-core/interfaces/, including LLMClient, ToolRegistry, VectorStoreAdapter, GraphStoreAdapter, and ContextEngineeringInterface.

All protocols use typing.Protocol with @runtime_checkable so that implementations can be validated at runtime without inheriting from an abstract base class.

@runtime_checkable
class ToolDefinition(Protocol):
    """Abstract representation of a tool capability."""

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """
        Unique tool identifier.
        Convention: lowercase_with_underscores
        Examples: "file_read", "web_search", "code_format"
        """
        ...

    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        """
        Human-readable description for the LLM.
        Should explain:
        - What the tool does
        - When to use it
        - What it returns
        """
        ...

    @property
    def parameters_schema(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """
        JSON Schema (Draft 7+) defining the tool's parameters.
        Must include type information, descriptions, and required fields.

        Example:
            {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "File path to read"
                    },
                    "encoding": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "File encoding",
                        "default": "utf-8"
                    }
                },
                "required": ["path"]
            }
        """
        ...

    @property
    def category(self) -> str:
        """
        Tool category for grouping and filtering.
        Standard: filesystem, shell, web, git, code, data, text, utility
        Defaults to "uncategorized".
        """
        ...

    @property
    def tags(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        Optional tags for fine-grained filtering.
        Examples: ["read-only", "safe"], ["async", "requires-auth"]
        """
        ...

    async def execute(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
        """
        Execute the tool with the given arguments.
        Must be async. Returns a string that is fed back to the LLM.
        kwargs names and types must match parameters_schema.
        """
        ...

    def to_schema(self, format: str = "plain") -> dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Convert to LLM function-calling format.

        "plain" format:
            {"name": ..., "description": ..., "parameters": {...}}

        "openai" format:
            {"type": "function", "function": {"name": ..., ...}}
        """
        ...

Implementation requirements:

  1. Tool names must be unique within a registry
  2. Descriptions must be clear enough for LLM decision-making
  3. Parameter schemas must be valid JSON Schema
  4. execute() must be async
  5. execute() must return a str

class LLMClient(Protocol):
    """Abstract interface for LLM inference."""

    async def chat_completion(
        self,
        messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
        tools: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
        response_model: type[BaseModel] | None = None,
        temperature: float = 0.7,
    ) -> ChatCompletionResponse:
        """
        Unified chat completion with optional tool calling.

        Args:
            messages: List of message dicts with 'role' and 'content'.
                     Supported roles: system, user, assistant, tool.

            tools: Optional list of tool schemas in OpenAI format:
                   [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": ..., ...}}]

            response_model: Optional Pydantic model for structured output.
                           If provided, response.content is parsed into this model.

            temperature: Sampling temperature (0.0 = deterministic, 1.0 = creative).

        Returns:
            ChatCompletionResponse:
            - If the LLM returns text: response.content contains text
            - If the LLM calls tools: response.tool_calls is populated
            - Use response.has_tool_calls to check

        Raises:
            LLMError: If the call fails after retries
            ValidationError: If response doesn't match response_model
        """
        ...

from friday_core.interfaces import LLMClient, ChatCompletionResponse, TokenUsage

class MyCustomLLMClient:
    """Custom LLM client implementing the LLMClient protocol."""

    async def chat_completion(
        self,
        messages: list[dict],
        tools: list[dict] | None = None,
        response_model=None,
        temperature: float = 0.7,
    ) -> ChatCompletionResponse:
        # Call your custom backend here
        raw = await my_backend.complete(messages, temperature=temperature)

        return ChatCompletionResponse(
            content=raw["text"],
            tool_calls=[],
            usage=TokenUsage(
                prompt_tokens=raw["input_tokens"],
                completion_tokens=raw["output_tokens"],
                total_tokens=raw["input_tokens"] + raw["output_tokens"],
            ),
            model="my-custom-model",
        )

from friday_core.interfaces import VectorStoreAdapter, SearchResult

class MyVectorStore:
    """Custom vector store (e.g., wrapping Pinecone or Weaviate)."""

    async def add(self, text: str, metadata: dict, collection: str = "default") -> str:
        embedding = await self._embed(text)
        doc_id = await self._backend.upsert(embedding, metadata, namespace=collection)
        return doc_id

    async def search(self, query: str, n_results: int = 5, ...) -> list[SearchResult]:
        query_embedding = await self._embed(query)
        raw_results = await self._backend.query(query_embedding, top_k=n_results)
        return [
            SearchResult(
                id=r["id"],
                content=r["metadata"]["text"],
                metadata=r["metadata"],
                score=r["score"],
                collection=collection,
            )
            for r in raw_results["matches"]
        ]

Protocol Design Principles

All Friday protocols follow these design principles established in ADR-001:

  1. Zero vendor lock-in — Swap any component by implementing the protocol
  2. Testability — Mock any protocol in unit tests without complex setup
  3. Clear contracts — Protocols document exact requirements for implementors
  4. Async throughout — All I/O methods are async def
  5. Pydantic at boundaries — Input/output types use Pydantic for validation

class FridayBaseSettings(BaseSettings):
    """Global settings inherited by all packages."""

    APP_ENV: str = "development"   # development | production | testing
    LOG_LEVEL: str = "INFO"        # DEBUG | INFO | WARNING | ERROR | CRITICAL
    DEFAULT_MODEL: str = "gpt-4-turbo"
    OPENAI_API_KEY: str | None = None
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: str | None = None

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_file=".env",
        env_file_encoding="utf-8",
        extra="ignore",
    )

Configuration Loading Priority

Settings are applied in this order (later overrides earlier):

  1. Default values in Pydantic model definitions
  2. .env file in the project root
  3. Environment variables (highest priority at startup)
  4. Runtime overrides via code

Environment Variable Naming

All Friday configuration keys can be set via environment variables using the FRIDAY_ prefix and double-underscore (__) nesting notation:

FRIDAY_<SECTION>__<SUBSECTION>__<SETTING>

Common environment variables:

Environment Variable Config Path Example
OPENAI_API_KEY llm.openai_api_key sk-proj-...
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY llm.anthropic_api_key sk-ant-...
OLLAMA_BASE_URL llm.ollama.base_url http://localhost:11434
FRIDAY_LLM__MODEL llm.model gpt-4o
FRIDAY_LLM__TEMPERATURE llm.temperature 0.7
FRIDAY_LLM__MAX_TOKENS llm.max_tokens 4096
FRIDAY_LLM__RESILIENCE__MAX_RETRIES llm.resilience.max_retries 5
FRIDAY_MEMORY__CONTEXT__MAX_TOKENS memory.context.max_tokens 8192
FRIDAY_MEMORY__PRIMING__ENABLED memory.priming.enabled true
FRIDAY_MEMORY__PRIMING__TOP_ENTITIES memory.priming.top_entities 50
FRIDAY_MEMORY__VECTOR__PROVIDER memory.vector.provider chroma
FRIDAY_MEMORY__GRAPH__PROVIDER memory.graph.provider networkx
FRIDAY_TOOLS__SECURITY__ENABLE_SANDBOX tools.security.enable_sandbox true
FRIDAY_EXTRACTION__ENABLED extraction.enabled true
FRIDAY_TRANSCRIPT__ENABLED transcript.enabled true
NEO4J_PASSWORD memory.graph.neo4j.password —
POSTGRES_PASSWORD memory.episodic.postgres.password —
REDIS_PASSWORD performance.caching.redis.password —
MCP_API_KEY mcp.server.api_key —
APP_ENV app.env production
LOG_LEVEL app.log_level WARNING

Type conversion rules:

  • Booleans: "true", "false", "1", "0", "yes", "no" (case-insensitive)
  • Numbers: Parsed as int or float based on decimal point presence
  • Lists: Comma-separated values: "item1,item2,item3"
  • None/Null: "null", "none", or empty string

Schema Sections Overview

The complete config.yaml is divided into these top-level sections:

Section Purpose
app Environment, log level, telemetry
llm Model, API keys, resilience, fallback
memory.context Token budget, budget strategy
memory.priming Entity loading, insight loading, recency
memory.lifecycle Decay, consolidation, pruning
memory.vector Vector store provider, collection, HNSW
memory.graph Graph store provider, Hebbian learning
memory.episodic Conversation history provider
extraction Entity/relationship/insight extraction
tools Selection strategy, allowlist, blocklist, security
agent CopilotAgent and AutonomousAgent settings
workflow Workflow engine, orchestration
transcript Recording settings, export, retention
mcp MCP server and client settings
security Secrets, input validation, rate limiting
performance Caching, concurrency, resource limits
development Debug mode, profiling, mock services
